newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: CSFB to set $40 mln FRN for Lithuanian refinery.
newsitem.headline: CSFB to set $40 mln FRN for Lithuanian refinery.

text.p: Credit Suisse First Boston (CSFB) is to be part of a group who will launch a $40 million Floating Rate Note (FRN) for Lithuanian refinery Mazheikiu Nafta after a contract has been signed this week, financial officials said on Wednesday.
A refinery spokeswoman confirmed the company wanted to raise $40 million but declined to give any details on the managing agent or the type of security that will sold.
But Lithuanian financial officials, who declined to be indentified, said the issue would be an FRN and would be arranged by CSFB and another bank.
It would be the first FRN for a Lithuanian issuer after the government launched two eurobonds.
"Mazheikiu Nafta expects the money to be transferred not long after the contract is signed and the funds will be used to buy crude oil supplies", the spokeswoman told Reuters.
"The terms of the contract say that the loan is to be paid back in seven months," the spokesman added.
The funds from the issue will be used to buy Russian crude oil.
Supplies of crude to Mazheikiu are often interrupted and the refinery recently has to shut down completly as it ran out of product to process.
